data.hypothesis: For large inputs, a 2048-element tile with 128-thread CTA reductions should produce far fewer partials than the baseline's repeated shrinking stages; a single CTA can finalize those partials in one second launch. This tests whether fewer stages outweigh the single-CTA finalizer's work, without assuming a speedup. Small inputs use a one-CTA path (or a direct operation for n=0/1) to avoid paying for a two-pass hierarchy.
data.notes: The supplied baseline is valid and correct, with three full-program samples averaging 46.244 microseconds. Its n=4,194,304 path performs four reduction launches plus a device-to-device copy. This candidate has not been measured; correctness and repeated full-program timing remain for the controller to evaluate. Every first-pass partial is written before finalization, tails are bounded, and 64-bit accumulation safely holds sums of int inputs for any nonnegative int n; the ABI and implicit default-stream ordering are preserved.
transformations: Replace the iterative multi-stage shrinking reduction with a two-pass hierarchy for n > 2048: one CTA per 2048-element tile writes a 64-bit partial, then one CTA reduces the partials directly to output.
Use a single 128-thread CTA for 1 < n <= 2048; produce the empty sum with a default-stream asynchronous memset and copy the sole input element directly for n == 1.
Accumulate thread-local, CTA, and final sums in 64-bit integers; bound each tile's tail and read only partials written by the current invocation.
